newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler finds new car, truck bosses in own backyard.
newsitem.headline: Daimler finds new car, truck bosses in own backyard.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG has turned to three Mercedes executives to take over the group's car- and truckmaking duties in the aftermath of a sweeping reorganisation announced on Thursday.
Under a plan approved by Daimler's supervisory board, Mercedes-Benz, one of the most profitable carmakers in the world, is to be legally dissolved as of April 1 and merged into the group structure.

Responsibilities previously held by Mercedes-Benz AG chairman Helmut Werner, who announced his resignation last Thursday, are to be split into three areas, each having a seat on the group's new management board.

"The new structure is a milestone in the drive to increase the company's earnings potential and will provide a more flexible framework for the further evolution of our business portfolio," Daimler chairman Juergen Schrempp said in a statement.
The revamp, designed to bring Daimler's core transport business closer to top management, created board positions for passenger cars, commercial vehicles sales and marketing.
In each case, Daimler turned to the Mercedes-Benz management board, choosing heads of individual business units to take newly created seats in the group's boardroom.

Juergen Hubbert, a Daimler employee since 1965 and an engineer by training, will take over the board position responsible for passenger cars -- a business that produced revenues of more than 40 billion marks in 1995.
The new car chief had been a member of Mercedes-Benz AG's management board since its founding in 1989 and was head of the passenger car division since February 1990.
Kurt Lauk, meanwhile, will continue to head up commercial vehicles, a post he has held since August 1996 when he replaced Bernd Gottschalk, who resigned in a dispute over strategy.

Lauk, who holds an MBA from Stanford University, is the only new board member without a long career behind him at Daimler. Before joining the group, he was chief financial officer at Veba AG and prior to that had worked for the Boston Consulting Group.

A third new board position, for sales and marketing, is to be taken over by Dieter Zetsche. Zetsche held overseas posts in Argentina and the U.S. and climbed the company ladder in product development rather than purely in marketing.

He became a deputy member of Mercedes-Benz's management board in April 1992, responsible for passenger car development and became a formal member of the board in July 1995, representing the sales division.

Former Mercedes chairman Werner had fought to keep Daimler's car and truck operations independent from the rest of the group, a desire Daimler management said they sought to address in designing the restructure.

While Mercedes will be merged with the group, Daimler's two other major units, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) and financial services and information technologies unit Debis AG, will remain full, legal companies.
Werner said that in the end, however, there was no room for someone of his experience in the new organisation.
